nodes.notes: PROBLEM: ConvBlock fp16 with quantize=False, integer_forward=False. Forward: conv2d(3x3, pad=1, stride=1, bias=True, in=16, out=32) -> ReLU -> AvgPool2d(2). Input shape (1,16,720,1280) fp16. Output (1,32,360,640) fp16. SECTIONS: 1) Classification: small conv (in=16,out=32,3x3) + elementwise relu + 2x2 avgpool; bandwidth-bound elementwise-stencil mixed. No reductions across batch. 2) Canonical: y[c_out,h,w]=sum_{c_in,kh,kw} x[c_in,h+kh-1,w+kw-1]*W[c_out,c_in,kh,kw]+b[c_out]; relu; pool: avg over 2x2 block. Can fuse all stages: produce 4 conv outputs per output pixel of pool then avg. 3) Layout: NCHW contiguous fp16. Weights 32*16*3*3=4608 fp16 elements, fits in shared/registers. Input read with 3x3 stencil (~9 reads per pixel). 4) Regimes: a) full 720x1280 -> BW-bound; b) tiny H/W -> launch overhead; c) different C -> mapping change. 5) Knobs: tile (BLOCK_H,BLOCK_W) per program covering 2x2 pool stride, tile over C_out (full 32 fits), unroll C_in=16, use shared/const weights, fuse relu+pool. 6) Skeleton: each program computes a tile of pooled output (tile_h,tile_w) for all 32 c_out: load weights (small), load input region (tile_h*2+2)*(tile_w*2+2)*16, compute 4 conv outputs per pool cell, relu, average, store. 7) Families: A) fused conv+relu+avgpool single Triton kernel with weights in registers/const; B) im2col + tensor-core matmul via tl.dot then fused relu+pool; C) two-stage: triton conv->relu and triton avgpool. Family A favored due to small C and BW-bound.

action.description: Single Triton kernel computing conv2d(3x3,pad=1) + bias + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2) fused. Each program computes a (BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W) tile of pooled output across all 32 output channels. Weights/bias loaded once per program. Use fp16 loads/stores and fp32 accumulation.
action.rationale: Fuses 3 ops, eliminates intermediates ~14MB+30MB, leverages small C_in/C_out fitting in registers.

kernel_summary: Fused fp16 conv-block: Conv2d(in=16,out=32,k=3,pad=1,stride=1,bias=True) -> ReLU -> AvgPool2d(2x2) on input (1,16,720,1280). Bandwidth-bound due to small channel counts and tiny weight tensor (~9KB). Output is (1,32,360,640) fp16 (~14MB). Key opportunity is to fuse all three ops in a single Triton kernel, hold weights in registers/constant, and avoid materializing the conv and post-relu intermediates. Tensor core use offers limited gains because N=C_out=32 is small. Main constraints: zero padding, fp16 dtype with fp32 accumulation, and per-program register budget when tiling across (H,W) and 32 output channels.
open_questions: Is the conv weight tensor stable across calls (constant) so it can be cached/pre-loaded into a fp16 const buffer?
What is cuDNN's baseline latency on RTX5090 for this conv shape (to estimate headroom)?
Can we tile fully across all 32 output channels in registers, or must we tile c_out (e.g., 16+16)?
Will fp32 accumulation be required for numerical match, or does fp16 accum pass tolerance?
Best (BLOCK_H, BLOCK_W) for pooled output: tradeoff between halo reuse and register pressure?
Does padding_mode='zeros' allow us to use boundary masks efficiently without branching?
Are there alignment guarantees on H,W (720,1280 are divisible by 16/32) that enable vectorized loads?
Should bias be loaded into shared memory once per program or broadcast via tl.load each tile?
